pr_title: Create a timeout that happens before cleanup
pr_body:
I know that I did this wrong, but the redis commands for setting, getting and deleting the flag are correct (I think). I just don't think I implemented the best solution or understood the problem well enough.

Closes #5435
pr_comments: It's a one liner based on the return value of set.
I think it's as simple as `return unless Sidekiq.redis { |c| c.set(...) }`.

issue_context.title: Minimize bootup time overhead
issue_context.body:
There are two places in sidekiq & sidekiq-pro which do "heavy" operations on bootup. In our use case, we are running thousands of sidekiq processes, so this bootup overhead slams redis often and creates spikey load issues.

In sidekiq: `Sidekiq::ProcessSet.cleanup` method
In sidekiq-pro: `Sidekiq::Pro::SuperFetch.cleanup_the_dead`

**Fix:** we discussed the fix for this as adding a 1 minute time-based lock/guard to throttle these methods from running too often. (It would be great if the lock seconds was a configurable option, so that we could tune this for our needs if needed)
comments: I'll fix Sidekiq Pro, Sam's going to tackle the ProcessSet fix.

Thanks very much @mperham and @SamArdrey !

Looking forward to upgrading this week once released and trying this out in prod.

I just looked and 6.5.2 has more changes in it than I remembered so I will do a release. Thanks for the poke.
@mperham do you have an ETA for the next sidekiq-pro release?

@mperham @SamArdrey just wanted to send you a note to say thanks! These simple changes in sidekiq & sidekiq-pro to throttle the bootup overhead had a fantastic impact on the redis DB in our large sidekiq deployment:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/75300/183760248-37644453-d2a2-4da6-8aa8-537c24290d8c.png)
^ we used to see spikes up to 150k ops/sec when autoscaling up many workers, now we rarely see 10k+ ops/sec

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/75300/183760627-2bd9edc1-eae1-482d-bf5a-1ca74b081763.png)
^ similarly, CPU would spike up to 80-100% and cause major redis latency issues and ops headaches, now we sit around 20% utilization

Huge impact, thanks for working through this with us and tackling this so quickly!

review_comments: Can you please make the 60 a constant for us, like CLEANUP_THROTTLE_SECONDS or something? Just in case we'd want to tune this more specifically, it'd be easier to inject (a la https://github.com/mperham/sidekiq/pull/5433/files)
I don't see the need to make this a knob. "Just in case" is not a usecase but you are welcome to open an issue if you have specific concerns or needs.
